findings.issue_text: [BUG] The light-theme (first) argument was silently changed from the original 30% to 70%: `color: dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 30%));` Reply-tab usernames in the small-actions area render at 70% lightness on light themes instead of the intended near-full-strength 30%, making them washed out; every other identical conversion in this PR keeps the original first argument, so this is a copy-paste error, not a deliberate change.

[BUG] The light-theme argument was inverted from the original 70% to 30%: `color: dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 70%));` The .custom-message-length hint in the mobile modal becomes near-black (30%) on light themes and near-white (70%) on dark themes, inverting the intended dimmed-subtext appearance; the parallel desktop/modal.scss site keeps 70%/30%, so this is an argument transposition error.

[BUG] The light-theme argument for h3 inside the onebox/title area was changed from 20% to 50%: `color: dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 50%));` The title heading loses its intended bold contrast on light mobile themes (50% instead of 20%), and the desktop twin at desktop/topic-post.scss:321 correctly keeps 20%/80%, so mobile users get visibly different (washed-out) title styling.

[BUG] The .name light-theme argument was changed from the original 30% to 50%: `color: dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 50%));` User-card names on desktop lose the darker 30% emphasis and become identical to the adjacent .title (50%) styling, flattening the visual hierarchy; the diff context shows the prior line was 30%.

[BUG] Same silent argument change as the desktop twin: .name was 30% and is now 50% in the light branch. Mobile user-card names render at 50% instead of 30% on light themes, losing the name-vs-title distinction the original stylesheet encoded.

[BUG] The light-theme branch of dark-light-choose was silently changed from 70% to 30% lightness, altering light-theme rendering in a PR that is supposed to be dark-theme-only. On light themes the .custom-message-length hint text drops from a 70%-lightness near-primary to a 30%-lightness heavy dark tone, visibly darkening modal hint text for all light-theme users — an unintended regression outside the PR's stated scope.

[BUG] The light-theme branch for the small-action bold link was changed from scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%) to 70%, dropping the original light-theme value. Light-theme users see the bolded small-action links (e.g. post-action links) rendered at 70% lightness instead of 30%, a much paler, lower-contrast color than before the PR — an unintended light-theme visual regression that also fails contrast against pale backgrounds.

[BUG] The light-theme branch for .staff .name was changed from scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%) to 50%, altering the light-theme color. Light-theme staff member names in the user page header render at 50% lightness instead of the previous 30%, losing the bold-name contrast the old stylesheet guaranteed — unintended regression on a path the PR claims not to touch.

[BUG] The light-theme branch for .staff .name was changed from scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%) to 50%, altering the light-theme color on mobile. Mobile light-theme staff names render at 50% instead of 30% lightness, a silent light-theme contrast regression mirroring the desktop one.

[BUG] The light-theme branch for h3 inside the topic-links / external-link block was changed from scale-color($primary, $lightness: 20%) to 50%, dropping the original dark heading color. On light themes the linked title heading in the topic footer renders at 50% lightness instead of 20%, a visibly paler, less heading-like color — unintended light-theme regression and an inconsistency with the desktop counterpart which kept 20%.

[ADVISORY] The adjacent .wmd-input rule still uses darken($primary, 40%) for text color on the same composer path being converted to dark-light-choose. In dark themes ($primary is light), darken($primary, 40%) makes the composer textarea text a murky dark gray on the dark disabled background — the exact bug class this PR fixes — left unconverted at the sibling selector on the very same rule block, so dark-theme composer input text stays broken.

[ADVISORY] The rule directly above the converted #draft-status still uses scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 50%) rather than dark-light-choose, leaving a mixed convention on the same composer block. Light-theme users get a $secondary-based (white-ish, near-invisible on a light background) color for that composer element while neighbors use $primary-based values, producing inconsistent and possibly unreadable text in the composer — the sibling-rule conversion was left incomplete.

[BUG] The light-theme branch's lightness was silently changed from 30% to 70% while converting to dark-light-choose, breaking the invariant that light-theme colors are unchanged by this PR. Light-theme users see the small-action links in the post stream jump from a dark 30%-tinted color to a washed-out 70%-tinted color, an unintended visual regression outside the stated intent (dark-theme fix only).

[BUG] .custom-message-length's light-theme branch was changed from 70% to 30% and the dark/light arguments are inverted relative to every other conversion in this PR (primary 30% / secondary 70%). Light-theme users get a much darker hint text than before, and dark-theme users get a 70%-tinted $secondary that is nearly invisible on a dark background — the opposite of the PR's goal, and inconsistent with the identical desktop/modal.scss rule which uses 70%/30%.

[BUG] The h3 (topic title in search/link results) lightness was changed from 20% to 50% in the light branch while converting, altering light-theme appearance. Light-theme users see the result h3 title change from a strong 20%-darkened color to a mid 50% tint, an unintended light-theme regression; the parallel desktop/topic-post.scss h3 correctly kept 20%/80%.

[BUG] .name's light branch was changed from 30% to 50% while converting to dark-light-choose, so the light and dark branches are now identical. Light-theme user names on the profile page lose their intended 30% emphasis and render at 50%, and the dark-light-choose wrapper is now a no-op (both arguments equal), indicating the conversion was botched rather than intentional.

[BUG] .name's light branch was changed from 30% to 50% while converting, making both branches of dark-light-choose identical. Light-theme mobile user names lose the 30% emphasis they had, and the wrapped call degenerates to a constant color, showing the change is not traceable to the stated dark-theme intent.

[ADVISORY] The PR's stated intent (all scale-color/darken-on-$primary usages must work on dark themes) is under-scoped: the adjacent `.wmd-input { color: darken($primary, 40%); }` and the untouched `color: scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 50%)` paths in the same file are not converted, so the dark-theme invariant is not enforced uniformly. Dark-theme users still get broken composer input text (darken($primary, 40%) on a dark $primary is near-invisible), leaving the diff's stated goal incompletely delivered within the very file it edits.

[BUG] The .name rule's primary lightness was silently changed from 30% to 50%, not just wrapped in dark-light-choose. On light themes the user profile name loses contrast relative to the bold .username above it (30% -> 50%), an unintended visual regression the PR title says nothing about.

[BUG] The mobile .name rule's primary lightness was changed from 30% to 50% instead of preserving the existing value inside dark-light-choose. Same contrast loss on light themes in the mobile user card/profile, and desktop+mobile .name rules now drift from their original 30% design value.

[BUG] The topic-map links rule changed primary lightness from 30% to 70% while being wrapped. On light themes these bold topic-map links go from a dark 30% tone to a washed-out 70% tone, making them nearly invisible against light backgrounds.

[BUG] The mobile topic-map h3 color changed primary lightness from 20% to 50% during the wrap. The mobile topic-map title drops from a very dark 20% tone to a mid 50% tone on light themes, a visible unintended de-emphasis and inconsistency with the desktop h3 (still 20%).

[BUG] .custom-message-length changed primary lightness from 70% to 30%, inverting the desktop/modal.scss counterpart which keeps 70%/30%. On light-theme mobile, the custom message length hint flips from a faint 70% tone to a strong dark 30% tone, while desktop shows the faint one — the same element renders with opposite weight on the two layouts, indicating a botched transcription rather than an intended change.

[ADVISORY] The coldmap-* rules wrap with dark-light-choose but the adjacent comment ("is scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%)") is now stale, and dark-light-choose uses the scheme's lightness threshold which depends on $primary/$secondary luminance, not on the same axis the coldmap ramp encodes. None

[BUG] The light-theme value was silently changed from 30% to 70% instead of being preserved: `a { font-weight: bold; color: dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 30%)); }` replaces `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)`. On light themes the user card action links (formerly a dark, emphasized 30% color) now render as a faint 70% tint, inverting the visual hierarchy — a behavior change to light themes that the PR title ('dark themes only') does not sanction and that no reviewer accepted.

[BUG] .name light-theme lightness was changed from 30% to 50%: `color: dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 50%));` replaces `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)`. On desktop light themes the user page display name loses its darker emphasis (30% → 50%), de-emphasizing a primary identity element on the user profile for all light-theme users — outside the stated dark-theme-only intent.

[BUG] .custom-message-length light-theme lightness was changed from 70% to 30% (the mirror value was applied to the primary branch instead of the secondary branch): `color: dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 70%));`. On mobile light themes the custom message character counter becomes a near-black 30% color instead of the intended faint 70% hint, and on dark themes it becomes a washed-out 70% tint — both branches regress versus the accepted pattern (desktop modal.scss keeps 70%/30%), producing inconsistent mobile vs desktop styling.

[BUG] The external-link h3 light-theme lightness was changed from 20% to 50%: `color: dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 50%));` replaces `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 20%)`. On mobile light themes the onebox/external-link title drops from a strong 20% heading color to a mid 50%, losing heading contrast; it also diverges from the parallel desktop rule (desktop/topic-post.scss h3 keeps 20%/80%), so mobile and desktop now render the same element with different weights.

[BUG] .name light-theme lightness was changed from 30% to 50%: `color: dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 50%));` replaces `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)`. On mobile light themes the user page display name loses its 30% emphasis and becomes the generic 50% muted color, de-emphasizing the identity element and diverging from the desktop counterpart where the same .name/.title pair was once uniformly 30%/50%.

[BUG] The small-action block link lightness was changed from 30% to 70% in the light-theme argument of dark-light-choose, altering light-theme rendering instead of only adding a dark-theme fallback. Everywhere else in this PR the light-theme value is preserved verbatim and only a $secondary dark variant is added; here light theme jumps from scale-color($primary, 30%) to 70%, so light-theme small-action links become much lighter than before the PR — a silent visual regression no test in the diff can catch.

[BUG] .custom-message-length was changed to dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 70%)), inverting both values relative to the desktop version (70%/30%). Desktop and mobile custom-message-length text diverge: mobile light-theme text darkens from 70% to 30% and dark-theme text lightens from the intended 70% to 30%-of-secondary — the mobile text is nearly the inverse of the desktop equivalent in both themes, contradicting the PR's stated goal of consistent dark-theme support.

[BUG] The h3 inside the small-action block was changed from scale-color($primary, 20%) to dark-light-choose(50%, 50%) instead of preserving the 20% light value. Mobile small-action h3 titles in the light theme lighten from 20% to 50%, breaking parity with desktop topic-post.scss (which keeps 20%/80% at the analogous h3) and silently changing light-theme appearance when the PR is scoped to dark-theme fixes.

[BUG] The .name rule was changed from scale-color($primary, 30%) to dark-light-choose(50%, 50%), replacing the light-theme value instead of preserving it. The user-card/profile .name in light theme loses its darker 30% tint and becomes 50% in both themes — the element is now visually indistinguishable from the adjacent .title (also 50%/50%), flattening the intended name/title hierarchy.

[BUG] Mobile .name mirrors the desktop change: 30% replaced by dark-light-choose(50%, 50%) instead of (30%, 70%). Mobile profile .name lightens from 30% to 50% in the light theme and collapses to the same value as .title, destroying the name/title visual distinction in both themes on mobile.

[BUG] The light-theme value for .custom-message-length was inverted from lightness 70% to 30% (dark-light-choose's first argument changed), whereas the equivalent desktop/modal.scss rule keeps 70%/30%. Light themes render the custom-message-length hint text at lightness 30% (dark, heavy) instead of the intended 70%, visibly changing light-mode modal appearance for every user with the light color scheme.

[BUG] The nested-post a link's light-theme value was changed from lightness 30% to 70% (scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%)) while every parallel rule (e.g. common/base/user.scss .username a at 30%/70%) keeps 30%. Light themes show nested-post usernames/links at 70% lightness (pale gray) instead of the previous 30%, degrading contrast for those links in all light color schemes — an unintended regression to light-mode styling in a PR scoped to dark themes.

[BUG] .name's light-theme color was changed from scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%) to 50% while common/base/user.scss .name keeps 30%, breaking the parallel between desktop and common definitions. Light themes render the user profile name at 50% lightness instead of 30%, so the desktop profile page shows the name paler than the shared/common styles intend — an unintended light-mode change shipped in a dark-theme PR.

[BUG] Mobile .name's light-theme color was changed from 30% to 50% lightness, diverging from the common/base/user.scss .name rule that retains 30%. On light themes, the mobile user profile name renders at 50% lightness instead of 30%, contradicting the shared user.scss rule and making the mobile and desktop/common renderings of the same element differ unintentionally.

[BUG] The link title h3's light-theme color was changed from lightness 20% to 50% while the parallel desktop/topic-post.scss h3 rule keeps 20%/80%. On light themes, mobile external-link titles render at 50% lightness instead of 20%, so they lose the bold dark heading emphasis they had before this PR — an unintended light-mode regression on every mobile link card.

[BUG] The light-theme branch of the small-action link color was changed from 30% to 70% lightness, making it identical to the dark-theme branch (70%/30% in both arguments), which is the opposite of the pattern used everywhere else in this diff where the light value is preserved verbatim. Small-action links in the post stream render at 70% lightness of $primary in light themes — near-invisible pale text on light backgrounds — instead of the previous readable 30%; this is the only hunk in the diff that alters the light-theme value, indicating a typo.

[BUG] The .custom-message-length lightness was changed from 70% to 30% while the desktop counterpart (desktop/modal.scss .custom-message-length) keeps 70%, and the dark branch here is 70% — both arguments are inverted relative to the consistent pattern. The custom message length hint in the mobile modal drops to 30% lightness of $primary in light themes (near-black heavy text where it was previously subtle), and the dark branch at 70% secondary is dimmer than intended; the mobile and desktop modals now render the same element with different colors.

[BUG] The light-theme branch of the small-action h3 color was changed from 20% to 50% lightness, while desktop/topic-post.scss keeps 20% for the same element — both branches of dark-light-choose are now 50%, making the dark/light distinction a no-op and diverging from desktop. The small-action heading (e.g. 'n votes') on mobile renders at 50% lightness in both themes, noticeably lighter than the 20% used on desktop for the same element, so mobile and desktop show different weights for identical content.

[ADVISORY] The .name color was changed from 30% to 50% lightness (both branches 50%), while the immediately adjacent common/base/user.scss .name keeps 30%/70% for the same element. The user-card name on desktop loses its 30%-vs-50% hierarchy versus .title and diverges from the common stylesheet's .name styling, so the same name element renders differently depending on which cascade wins; whoever audits badge/name contrast later must reconcile two now-different values.

[ADVISORY] The mobile user .name color was changed from 30% to 50% (both branches 50%), diverging from common/base/user.scss .name which keeps 30%/70%. Mobile user profiles render the name at a lighter weight than desktop/common for the same element, an inconsistency introduced only in this diff that the next color audit must catch by diffing three files.

adjudication.rationale: In `app/assets/stylesheets/mobile/topic-post.scss`, within the `a.star` block, the `h3` color was changed from `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 20%)` to `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 50%))`, which makes the light-theme branch 50% lightness instead of the original 20%. In the desktop counterpart (`app/assets/stylesheets/desktop/topic-post.scss`), the `h3` light-theme branch remains at 20% (`dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 20%), ...)`). This is a verifiable light-theme visual regression/inconsistency introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The adjacent .wmd-input rule still uses darken($primary, 40%) for text color on the same composer path being converted to dark-light-choose. In dark themes ($primary is light), darken($primary, 40%) makes the composer textarea text a murky dark gray on the dark disabled background — the exact bug class this PR fixes — left unconverted at the sibling selector on the very same rule block, so dark-theme composer input text stays broken.

adjudication.rationale: In `app/assets/stylesheets/mobile/compose.scss`, the composer block updates disabled backgrounds to `dark-light-choose(...)` (e.g. `#reply-title:disabled` and `.wmd-input:disabled`), but the sibling `.wmd-input { color: darken($primary, 40%); }` remains unchanged. The diff therefore shows an incomplete conversion in the same rule group; whether this causes the specific dark-theme contrast bug described cannot be fully verified from the diff alone (theme variable values aren’t shown), but the unconverted `darken($primary, 40%)` is real and directly relevant to the PR’s color-theme changes.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The rule directly above the converted #draft-status still uses scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 50%) rather than dark-light-choose, leaving a mixed convention on the same composer block. Light-theme users get a $secondary-based (white-ish, near-invisible on a light background) color for that composer element while neighbors use $primary-based values, producing inconsistent and possibly unreadable text in the composer — the sibling-rule conversion was left incomplete.

adjudication.rationale: In `app/assets/stylesheets/mobile/compose.scss`, the line immediately before the changed `#draft-status` rule still reads `color: scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 50%);` while `#draft-status` was converted to `dark-light-choose(...)`, so the finding about an incomplete/mixed convention in that composer block is grounded in the diff. However, the claim about an actual unreadable color for light-theme users is not directly verifiable from the diff alone (it depends on theme variable values), and the `$secondary`-based line itself was not introduced/changed by this PR, so this is better classified as an incomplete conversion/consistency issue rather than a definite new bug.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The light-theme branch's lightness was silently changed from 30% to 70% while converting to dark-light-choose, breaking the invariant that light-theme colors are unchanged by this PR. Light-theme users see the small-action links in the post stream jump from a dark 30%-tinted color to a washed-out 70%-tinted color, an unintended visual regression outside the stated intent (dark-theme fix only).

This change should be reviewed to ensure it aligns with design intentions.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] .custom-message-length's light-theme branch was changed from 70% to 30% and the dark/light arguments are inverted relative to every other conversion in this PR (primary 30% / secondary 70%). Light-theme users get a much darker hint text than before, and dark-theme users get a 70%-tinted $secondary that is nearly invisible on a dark background — the opposite of the PR's goal, and inconsistent with the identical desktop/modal.scss rule which uses 70%/30%.

adjudication.rationale: In `app/assets/stylesheets/mobile/modal.scss`, `.custom-message-length` was changed from `color: scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%);` to `color: dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 70%));`, which makes the light-theme (first) branch much darker than before (30% vs 70%). This is also inconsistent with the corresponding rule in `app/assets/stylesheets/desktop/modal.scss`, which uses `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 30%))`. The diff clearly shows a likely mistaken lightness swap for mobile.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] Mobile .name's light-theme color was changed from 30% to 50% lightness, diverging from the common/base/user.scss .name rule that retains 30%. On light themes, the mobile user profile name renders at 50% lightness instead of 30%, contradicting the shared user.scss rule and making the mobile and desktop/common renderings of the same element differ unintentionally.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows that in both `app/assets/stylesheets/desktop/user.scss` and `app/assets/stylesheets/mobile/user.scss`, the `.name` color was changed from `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)` to `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%), ...)`, i.e., the light-theme branch is now 50% lightness. Meanwhile `common/base/user.scss` keeps `.name` at 30% lightness in the light-theme branch (`dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%), ...)`). This verifies the inconsistency the finding points out. However, the diff alone doesn’t prove that using 50% on mobile is a correctness defect versus an intentional design adjustment, so it’s best treated as a specific, diff-grounded review concern about unintended divergence rather than a verifiable bug.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The link title h3's light-theme color was changed from lightness 20% to 50% while the parallel desktop/topic-post.scss h3 rule keeps 20%/80%. On light themes, mobile external-link titles render at 50% lightness instead of 20%, so they lose the bold dark heading emphasis they had before this PR — an unintended light-mode regression on every mobile link card.

adjudication.rationale: In app/assets/stylesheets/mobile/topic-post.scss, within `a.star h3`, the color changes from `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 20%)` to `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 50%))`, which directly alters the light-theme (primary) lightness from 20% to 50%. In the parallel desktop rule (app/assets/stylesheets/desktop/topic-post.scss, `a.star h3`), the new value remains aligned with the prior intent: `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 20%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 80%))`. This inconsistency is verifiable in the diff and plausibly indicates an unintended light-mode regression for mobile link-card titles.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The light-theme branch of the small-action link color was changed from 30% to 70% lightness, making it identical to the dark-theme branch (70%/30% in both arguments), which is the opposite of the pattern used everywhere else in this diff where the light value is preserved verbatim. Small-action links in the post stream render at 70% lightness of $primary in light themes — near-invisible pale text on light backgrounds — instead of the previous readable 30%; this is the only hunk in the diff that alters the light-theme value, indicating a typo.

adjudication.rationale: In `app/assets/stylesheets/desktop/topic-post.scss` around the `nav.post-controls` block (`@@ -288`), the link color inside `a { font-weight: bold; ... }` is changed from `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)` to `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 30%))`. This is the only shown hunk where the light-theme (first argument) lightness value is not preserved from the prior `scale-color(...)` value, unlike the rest of the diff which wraps the old value as the first argument. That makes the light-theme value much lighter (70% vs 30%), consistent with a likely typo and plausibly reducing contrast in light themes.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The .custom-message-length lightness was changed from 70% to 30% while the desktop counterpart (desktop/modal.scss .custom-message-length) keeps 70%, and the dark branch here is 70% — both arguments are inverted relative to the consistent pattern. The custom message length hint in the mobile modal drops to 30% lightness of $primary in light themes (near-black heavy text where it was previously subtle), and the dark branch at 70% secondary is dimmer than intended; the mobile and desktop modals now render the same element with different colors.

adjudication.rationale: In `app/assets/stylesheets/mobile/modal.scss`, `.custom-message-length` changed from `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%)` to `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 70%))`. This is inconsistent with the desktop counterpart (`app/assets/stylesheets/desktop/modal.scss`) which uses `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 30%))` and with the general pattern in the diff (lighter `$primary` for light themes, darker/lower-lightness `$secondary` for dark themes). The mobile modal’s arguments/lightness values are effectively inverted vs desktop, causing a clear cross-platform color mismatch for the same element.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The light-theme branch of the small-action h3 color was changed from 20% to 50% lightness, while desktop/topic-post.scss keeps 20% for the same element — both branches of dark-light-choose are now 50%, making the dark/light distinction a no-op and diverging from desktop. The small-action heading (e.g. 'n votes') on mobile renders at 50% lightness in both themes, noticeably lighter than the 20% used on desktop for the same element, so mobile and desktop show different weights for identical content.

adjudication.rationale: In `app/assets/stylesheets/mobile/topic-post.scss`, the `a.star h3` color was changed from `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 20%)` to `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 50%))`, i.e. both branches are `50%` lightness, making the dark/light choice effectively a no-op for lightness. In contrast, `app/assets/stylesheets/desktop/topic-post.scss` for the same `a.star h3` keeps a much darker light-theme value (`$lightness: 20%`) and a different dark-theme value, so mobile now diverges in a way that is visible and inconsistent per the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The .name color was changed from 30% to 50% lightness (both branches 50%), while the immediately adjacent common/base/user.scss .name keeps 30%/70% for the same element. The user-card name on desktop loses its 30%-vs-50% hierarchy versus .title and diverges from the common stylesheet's .name styling, so the same name element renders differently depending on which cascade wins; whoever audits badge/name contrast later must reconcile two now-different values.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `.name` in `common/base/user.scss` stays at primary lightness 30% via `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 70%))`, but `.name` in both `desktop/user.scss` and `mobile/user.scss` is changed from 30% to `dark-light-choose(...50%, ...50%)`. This creates a concrete, diff-grounded inconsistency between common styling and platform-specific overrides and may alter visual hierarchy/maintenance expectations, but it’s a UI/style divergence rather than a clearly verifiable functional defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The mobile user .name color was changed from 30% to 50% (both branches 50%), diverging from common/base/user.scss .name which keeps 30%/70%. Mobile user profiles render the name at a lighter weight than desktop/common for the same element, an inconsistency introduced only in this diff that the next color audit must catch by diffing three files.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `.name` color in both `app/assets/stylesheets/desktop/user.scss` and `app/assets/stylesheets/mobile/user.scss` changing from `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)` to `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 50%))`, while `app/assets/stylesheets/common/base/user.scss` keeps `.name` at `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 70%))`. That’s a concrete cross-file visual inconsistency introduced in this diff (though it affects desktop too, not only mobile), which is a real review concern but not a functional bug.
